### ⚑ Section A · Q2. · i. — 1 mark

> Abha Didi was a natural scientist.

- **Answer: True**
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.4 l.5

### ⚑ Section A · Q3. · iii. — 1 mark

> milk nuts grains fruits seeds

- Options: milk · nuts · grains · fruits · seeds
- **Answer: milk**
- Marking guide: Milk: the others are food from plants that birds eat (grains, berries, fruits, nuts in the food-picking activity).
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.13 l.2
- Teacher note: The rule behind the group is not stated; milk is the only food that does not come from plants and is not bird food. Accept milk.

### ⚑ Section A · Q3. · iv. — 1 mark

> fish snake frog turtle tiger

- Options: fish · snake · frog · turtle · tiger
- **Answer: tiger · fish**
- Marking guide: Tiger: the others are in the textbook list of animals that live in and around water. Fish is also accepted: it is the only one that lives only in water and cannot come onto land.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.16 l.1
- Teacher note: Two answers are defensible: tiger (not a water animal, intended) and fish (the only one that lives only in water). Both get full marks.

### ⚑ Section B · Q4. — 3 marks

> Match the following

- Pairs:
  - i. (picture i) → c. footprint of an animal
  - ii (picture ii) → a. webbed feet
  - iii. (picture iii) → b. beak of a bird
- **Answer: i - c (footprint of an animal); ii - a (webbed feet); iii - b (beak of a bird)**
- Answer points:
  - i (paw prints) - c. footprint of an animal (1 mark)
  - ii (webbed foot) - a. webbed feet (1 mark)
  - iii (hooked beak) - b. beak of a bird (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All three pictures matched correctly.
  - partial (2 marks): Two pictures matched correctly (1 mark each).
  - partial-low (1 mark): One picture matched correctly.
  - none (0 marks): No correct match.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.13 l.16
- Teacher note: On the printed sheet the numerals i, ii, iii sit beside the bottom of each picture, so it is unclear which picture each numeral belongs to ("ii" also has no full stop). Here the pictures are read top to bottom as i = paw prints, ii = webbed foot, iii = beak. If the child worked on the printout, mark by picture: paw prints - footprint, webbed foot - webbed feet, beak - beak of a bird.

### ⚑ Section B · Q5. · ii. — 1 mark

> An insect with three pairs of legs and one antennae

- **Answer: Grasshopper (or any insect)**
- Also accept: grasshopper · grasshoppers · ant · ants · beetle · beetles · bee · bees · honeybee · honey bee · housefly · house fly · fly · flies · butterfly · butterflies · moth · mosquito · mosquitoes · praying mantis · mantis · cockroach · dragonfly · ladybird · ladybug · termite · wasp · cricket · firefly · chinti · titli · makkhi · machchhar · tidda · jhingur
- Marking guide: Any insect gets the mark; the textbook example is the grasshopper.

### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · i. — 1 mark

> Where did the students get ready to go with their teacher?

- **Answer: For a nature trail at Pachmarhi, Madhya Pradesh.**
- Answer points:
  - A nature trail at Pachmarhi (Panchmarhi), Madhya Pradesh; "Pachmarhi" alone or "a nature trail in the forest" also gets the mark (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says Pachmarhi (any spelling) or a nature trail / the forest at Pachmarhi.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "a forest" or "a trip" without the place or the nature trail.
  - none (0 marks): Wrong place or blank.

### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · ii. — 1 mark

> Write two rules to be followed in a zoo or forest.

- **Answer: Any two: do not tease animals; do not feed animals; do not damage trees and flowers; do not throw garbage; do not bring polythene bags; do not bring pets or weapons; be careful in a new place; do not damage public utilities.**
- Answer points:
  - First sensible rule (e.g. do not tease or feed animals) (0.5 marks)
  - Second sensible rule (e.g. do not throw garbage, do not damage plants) (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two sensible rules.
  - partial (0.5 marks): One sensible rule.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible rule.
- Model answer: We should not feed the animals. We should not throw garbage in the forest.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.5 l.11

### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · iii. — 1 mark

> What special features do water animals have?

- **Answer: Fish have fins to swim; turtles have strong shells and webbed feet to swim; the gharial has a long, narrow, pointed snout to catch fish; frogs can live on land and in water.**
- Answer points:
  - One correct feature (fins, webbed feet, shell, pointed snout, gills, streamlined body) (0.5 marks)
  - A second correct feature (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two correct features (e.g. fins and webbed feet).
  - partial (0.5 marks): One correct feature.
  - none (0 marks): No correct feature.
- Model answer: Fish have fins to swim, and turtles have webbed feet and a strong shell.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.16 l.14

### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · iv. — 1 mark

> How do  leaves differ from one another?

- **Answer: Leaves differ in colour, shape, size and texture (smooth or rough), in the pattern of their veins, and in smell.**
- Answer points:
  - One way (shape, size, colour, texture, veins, smell) (0.5 marks)
  - A second way (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two or more ways (e.g. shape and colour).
  - partial (0.5 marks): One way.
  - none (0 marks): No correct way.
- Model answer: Leaves differ in their shape, size, colour and texture.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.19 l.8
- Teacher note: Printed with a double space in "How do  leaves"; kept as printed.

### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · v. — 1 mark

- **Answer: Any two: birds have feathers; a beak; two wings; two legs with claws; most can fly; they lay eggs.**

### ⚑ Section C · Q9. — 2 marks

> Draw a picture denoting the diversity of animals in a forest.

- **Answer: A forest scene (trees) with several different kinds of animals, e.g. a tiger, a deer, a monkey on a tree, birds, a snake, insects and a pond with fish or a frog.**
- Answer points:
  - Forest setting with trees or plants (1 mark)
  - At least four different kinds of animals (land, birds, insects, water) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): A forest setting with four or more different kinds of animals.
  - partial (1 mark): A forest setting with only two or three kinds of animals, or many animals with no forest shown.
  - weak (0.5 marks): Only one animal or only trees drawn.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing drawn, or the drawing does not show a forest or animals.
- Model answer: Trees and bushes, a deer and a tiger on the ground, a monkey on a branch, birds in the sky, a butterfly on a flower, and a pond with a fish and a frog.
- Marking guide: 1 mark: a forest setting (trees, plants). 1 mark: at least four different kinds of animals (for example a land animal, a bird, an insect and a water animal), showing diversity. Neatness and labels are a bonus, not required.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.18 l.1

- Teacher note: The question is oddly worded; the textbook line is "got ready for a nature trail at Pachmarhi". Accept Pachmarhi, Panchmarhi, or "a nature trail".

#### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · ii. — 1 mark

> Write two rules to be followed in a zoo or forest.

- **Answer: Any two: do not tease animals; do not feed animals; do not damage trees and flowers; do not throw garbage; do not bring polythene bags; do not bring pets or weapons; be careful in a new place; do not damage public utilities.**
- Answer points:
  - First sensible rule (e.g. do not tease or feed animals) (0.5 marks)
  - Second sensible rule (e.g. do not throw garbage, do not damage plants) (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two sensible rules.
  - partial (0.5 marks): One sensible rule.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible rule.
- Model answer: We should not feed the animals. We should not throw garbage in the forest.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.5 l.11

#### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · iii. — 1 mark

> What special features do water animals have?

- **Answer: Fish have fins to swim; turtles have strong shells and webbed feet to swim; the gharial has a long, narrow, pointed snout to catch fish; frogs can live on land and in water.**
- Answer points:
  - One correct feature (fins, webbed feet, shell, pointed snout, gills, streamlined body) (0.5 marks)
  - A second correct feature (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two correct features (e.g. fins and webbed feet).
  - partial (0.5 marks): One correct feature.
  - none (0 marks): No correct feature.
- Model answer: Fish have fins to swim, and turtles have webbed feet and a strong shell.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.16 l.14

#### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · iv. — 1 mark

> How do  leaves differ from one another?

- **Answer: Leaves differ in colour, shape, size and texture (smooth or rough), in the pattern of their veins, and in smell.**
- Answer points:
  - One way (shape, size, colour, texture, veins, smell) (0.5 marks)
  - A second way (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two or more ways (e.g. shape and colour).
  - partial (0.5 marks): One way.
  - none (0 marks): No correct way.
- Model answer: Leaves differ in their shape, size, colour and texture.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.19 l.8
- Teacher note: Printed with a double space in "How do  leaves"; kept as printed.

#### ⚑ Section B · Q6. · v. — 1 mark

> Write two characteristic features of a bird.

- **Answer: Any two: birds have feathers; a beak; two wings; two legs with claws; most can fly; they lay eggs.**
- Answer points:
  - First feature (feathers, beak, wings, claws, two legs, lays eggs, can fly) (0.5 marks)
  - Second feature (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Two correct features.
  - partial (0.5 marks): One correct feature.
  - none (0 marks): No correct feature.
- Model answer: A bird has feathers and a beak.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.13 l.16

**Q9. — Draw a picture denoting the diversity of animals in a forest. (2)**

#### ⚑ Section C · Q9. — 2 marks

> Draw a picture denoting the diversity of animals in a forest.

- **Answer: A forest scene (trees) with several different kinds of animals, e.g. a tiger, a deer, a monkey on a tree, birds, a snake, insects and a pond with fish or a frog.**
- Answer points:
  - Forest setting with trees or plants (1 mark)
  - At least four different kinds of animals (land, birds, insects, water) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): A forest setting with four or more different kinds of animals.
  - partial (1 mark): A forest setting with only two or three kinds of animals, or many animals with no forest shown.
  - weak (0.5 marks): Only one animal or only trees drawn.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing drawn, or the drawing does not show a forest or animals.
- Model answer: Trees and bushes, a deer and a tiger on the ground, a monkey on a branch, birds in the sky, a butterfly on a flower, and a pond with a fish and a frog.
- Marking guide: 1 mark: a forest setting (trees, plants). 1 mark: at least four different kinds of animals (for example a land animal, a bird, an insect and a water animal), showing diversity. Neatness and labels are a bonus, not required.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.18 l.1
